plan.root_cause: The datepicker does not hide when the input field loses focus via tab navigation, because there is no blur event listener to trigger the hide.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a blur event listener to the input field that calls the datepicker's hide() method.

const listeners = [
      [inputField, 'keydown', onKeydown.bind(null, this)],
      [inputField, 'focus', onFocus.bind(null, this)],
      [inputField, 'mousedown', onMousedown.bind(null, this)],
      [inputField, 'click', onClickInput.bind(null, this)],
      [inputField, 'paste', onPaste.bind(null, this)],
      [inputField, 'blur', this._onBlur.bind(this)],
      [document, 'mousedown', onMousedownDocument],
      [document, 'touchstart', onMousedownDocument],
      [window, 'resize', picker.place.bind(picker)]
    ];

plan.expected_accessibility_effect: When the user tabs away from the date input field, the datepicker will close, ensuring that it does not obscure subsequent content and allowing assistive technologies to navigate the page correctly.
functional_risks: Hiding the picker on blur may cause the picker to disappear if the user intends to interact with it via an assistive technology that simulates focus loss without actual user intent to leave the field.
If the picker is made focusable in the future (e.g., by adding tabindex to its elements), the blur listener might hide it prematurely when navigating into the picker via keyboard.
verification_requirements: Tabbing away from the date input field with a valid date should update the form data and hide the datepicker.
Tabbing away from the date input field with an invalid date (outside min/max) should hide the datepicker without updating the form data.
Clicking on the datepicker buttons should not cause the picker to hide unexpectedly.
The datepicker should still hide when clicking outside the picker (via the existing onClickOutside listener).

plan.root_cause: The Datepicker class lacks a _onBlur method to handle blur events on the input field, and lacks a hide method to delegate to the picker. The blur event listener is registered but calls a non-existent method, so the datepicker does not hide when the user tabs away.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a hide method to the Datepicker class that calls this.picker.hide(), and add an _onBlur method that conditionally calls this.update() based on the updateOnBlur config, then calls this.hide().
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: When the user tabs away from the date input field, the datepicker will close, ensuring that it does not obscure subsequent content and allowing assistive technologies to navigate the page correctly.
functional_risks: Hiding the picker on blur may cause the picker to disappear if the user intends to interact with it via an assistive technology that simulates focus loss without actual user intent to leave the field.
If the picker is made focusable in the future (e.g., by adding tabindex to its elements), the blur listener might hide it prematurely when navigating into the picker via keyboard.
verification_requirements: Tabbing away from the date input field with a valid date should update the form data and hide the datepicker.
Tabbing away from the date input field with an invalid date (outside min/max) should hide the datepicker without updating the form data.
Clicking on the datepicker buttons should not cause the picker to hide unexpectedly.

plan.root_cause: The Datepicker class lacks a _onBlur method to handle blur events on the input field. The blur event listener is registered in the constructor but calls a non-existent method, so the datepicker does not hide when the user tabs away.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a _onBlur method that checks if focus moved into the picker (to avoid hiding when clicking the picker), and if not, calls this.update() which will update the selection from the input field and hide the picker (since update uses autohide: true by default).
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: When the user tabs away from the date input field, the datepicker will close, ensuring it does not obscure subsequent content and allowing assistive technologies to navigate the page correctly.
functional_risks: If the picker is made focusable in the future, the blur listener might hide it prematurely when navigating into the picker via keyboard.
The update() call on blur will revert the input field value if the typed date is invalid (outside min/max), which is the desired behavior per requirements.
verification_requirements: Tabbing away from the date input field with a valid date should update the form data and hide the datepicker.
Tabbing away from the date input field with an invalid date (outside min/max) should hide the datepicker without updating the form data (reverting to previous valid date).
Clicking on the datepicker buttons should not cause the picker to hide unexpectedly.
The datepicker should still hide when clicking outside the picker (via the existing onClickOutside listener).
